text: Because your brain sees it coming.
Every time you move, your brain predicts what that movement will feel like.
A part called the cerebellum sends out that prediction, and the feeling gets turned down.
Tickling needs surprise. If the touch is predicted, there's no surprise.
Scientists tested this with a tickle robot. When people moved it themselves, it barely tickled.
But add a tiny delay, a fraction of a second, and it started to tickle more.
So try it right now. Nothing, right?
